chunks: "The basic types are integers, characters, floating-point numbers, booleans and pointers.
In C, an integer type like int or short stores a whole number in a fixed number of bits, signed or unsigned. A char is a small integer, usually 8 bits, used for characters.
float and double store real numbers in IEEE 754 format, 32 and 64 bits. bool holds true or false, and a pointer holds a memory address. The important thing for hardware is size.
The size of int depends on the platform, 16 bits on some microcontrollers and 32 on most others, so in firmware I use fixed-width types like uint8 t , uint16 t and int32 t .
An 8-bit unsigned goes from 0 to 255, a 16-bit from 0 to 65,535, a 32-bit up to about 4. 29 billion. Signed types use two's complement, so int8 goes from minus 128 to 127.
Two things bite people. Overflow: an unsigned 8-bit 250 plus 10 wraps to 4, and signed overflow is actually undefined in C.
And floating point: a float has about 7 decimal digits of precision, so 0. 1 + 0. 2 isn't exactly 0. 3 , and a float can't count above 16. 7 million in steps of one.
In Python, types belong to values and are checked at runtime, integers have arbitrary size, and float is a 64-bit double."
